# References

Every empirical number in INA-sim traces to an entry here. `access` records how it entered the repo: **verbatim** (equation transcribed from the source text), **derived** (computed here from the source's tabulated measurements, with the script named), or **textbook** (standard constant or relation).

Generated from INA-sim 0.3.1. Also available as `ina-sim refs`.

## Harrison et al. (2019)

`harrison2019` · access: **verbatim** · open access

Harrison, A. D., Lever, K., Sanchez-Marroquin, A., Holden, M. A., Whale, T. F., Tarn, M. D., McQuaid, J. B., Murray, B. J. (2019). The ice-nucleating ability of quartz immersed in water and its atmospheric importance compared to K-feldspar. Atmospheric Chemistry and Physics 19, 11343-11361. doi:10.5194/acp-19-11343-2019

<https://acp.copernicus.org/articles/19/11343/2019/>

**Used for:** Source of the K-feldspar, quartz, plagioclase feldspar and albite ns(T) polynomials. All four fits are on BET-derived surface area. The paper states the sigma of log10(ns) for each fit; those are carried through as the uncertainty of every derived quantity.

**Cited by:** anchor `mineral_activity_ordering`, parameterization `albite_harrison2019`, parameterization `k_feldspar_harrison2019`, parameterization `plagioclase_harrison2019`, parameterization `quartz_harrison2019`

## Niemand et al. (2012)

`niemand2012` · access: **verbatim** · paywalled

Niemand, M., Mohler, O., Vogel, B., Vogel, H., Hoose, C., Connolly, P., Klein, H., Bingemer, H., DeMott, P., Skrotzki, J., Leisner, T. (2012). A particle-surface-area-based parameterization of immersion freezing on desert dust particles. Journal of the Atmospheric Sciences 69, 3077-3092. doi:10.1175/JAS-D-11-0249.1

**Used for:** AIDA chamber desert dust immersion INAS fit ns(T) = exp(8.934 - 0.517 T), T in degrees Celsius, ns in m^-2, valid -36 to -12 C. The paper itself is paywalled; coefficients were taken from the verbatim restatement in Kanji et al. (2019), ACP 19, 5091-5110 (doi:10.5194/acp-19-5091-2019), p. 5103: "a = 8.934, b = -0.517, and T is measured in degrees Celsius". Surface area basis is the aerosol geometric surface area from the AIDA size distributions, NOT BET.

**Cited by:** parameterization `desert_dust_niemand2012`

## Murray et al. (2011)

`murray2011` · access: **verbatim** · open access

Murray, B. J., Broadley, S. L., Wilson, T. W., Atkinson, J. D., Wills, R. H. (2011). Heterogeneous freezing of water droplets containing kaolinite particles. Atmospheric Chemistry and Physics 11, 4191-4207. doi:10.5194/acp-11-4191-2011

<https://acp.copernicus.org/articles/11/4191/2011/>

**Used for:** Source of the time-dependent (stochastic) description used here: Eq. (24) heterogeneous nucleation rate coefficient for kaolinite KGa-1b, Eq. (23) homogeneous nucleation rate coefficient for pure water (itself taken from Murray et al. 2010), and Eqs. (16)-(19), the multi-component survival-probability model that turns rate coefficients into a frozen fraction.

**Cited by:** anchor `kaolinite_rate_at_239k`, parameterization `kaolinite_murray2011`

## Murray et al. (2010)

`murray2010` · access: **verbatim** · paywalled

Murray, B. J., Broadley, S. L., Wilson, T. W., Bull, S. J., Wills, R. H., Christenson, H. K., Murray, E. J. (2010). Kinetics of the homogeneous freezing of water. Physical Chemistry Chemical Physics 12, 10380-10387. doi:10.1039/c003297b

**Used for:** Origin of the homogeneous nucleation rate coefficient J_hom(T) that Murray et al. (2011) restate as their Eq. (23); the coefficients used here are transcribed from that open-access restatement.

**Cited by:** parameterization `water_homogeneous_murray2010`

## Marcolli et al. (2016)

`marcolli2016` · access: **derived** · open access

Marcolli, C., Nagare, B., Welti, A., Lohmann, U. (2016). Ice nucleation efficiency of AgI: review and new insights. Atmospheric Chemistry and Physics 16, 8915-8937. doi:10.5194/acp-16-8915-2016

<https://acp.copernicus.org/articles/16/8915/2016/>

**Used for:** Table 1 compiles 60 years of AgI immersion-freezing experiments as (particle diameter, particles per droplet, activated fraction, freezing temperature). INA-sim inverts those rows to ns(T) with the singular approximation of Vali (1971) and fits log10(ns) linearly in T. Raw rows live in src/ina_sim/validation/datasets/agi_marcolli2016_table1.yaml; the fit is regenerated by tools/fit_agi_ns.py. AgI has no published INAS parameterization comparable to the mineral fits, so this is the honest substitute and is labelled derived, not published.

**Cited by:** anchor `agi_band_covers_measurements_2sigma`, anchor `agi_band_covers_measurements`, parameterization `agi_marcolli2016_derived`

## Vali (1971)

`vali1971` · access: **textbook** · paywalled

Vali, G. (1971). Quantitative evaluation of experimental results on the heterogeneous freezing nucleation of supercooled liquids. Journal of the Atmospheric Sciences 28, 402-409. doi:10.1175/1520-0469(1971)028<0402:QEOERA>2.0.CO;2

**Used for:** The cumulative nucleus spectrum and the singular inversion ns = -ln(1 - f_ice) / A used throughout this repo.

## Vali et al. (2015)

`vali2015` · access: **verbatim** · open access

Vali, G., DeMott, P. J., Mohler, O., Whale, T. F. (2015). Technical Note: A proposal for ice nucleation terminology. Atmospheric Chemistry and Physics 15, 10263-10270. doi:10.5194/acp-15-10263-2015

<https://acp.copernicus.org/articles/15/10263/2015/>

**Used for:** Terminology standard followed by this repo: "ice nucleating particle (INP)" rather than "ice nucleus", and ns(T) with dimension L^-2. Quoted at p. 10267: the quantity "is designated as ns(T), or ns(S), with dimension of L^-2 (CGS units of cm^-2)".

## Hoose and Mohler (2012)

`hoose2012` · access: **verbatim** · open access

Hoose, C., Mohler, O. (2012). Heterogeneous ice nucleation on atmospheric aerosols: a review of results from laboratory experiments. Atmospheric Chemistry and Physics 12, 9817-9854. doi:10.5194/acp-12-9817-2012

## Atkinson et al. (2013)

`atkinson2013` · access: **verbatim** · paywalled

Atkinson, J. D., Murray, B. J., Woodhouse, M. T., Whale, T. F., Baustian, K. J., Carslaw, K. S., Dobbie, S., O'Sullivan, D., Malkin, T. L. (2013). The importance of feldspar for ice nucleation by mineral dust in mixed-phase clouds. Nature 498, 355-358. doi:10.1038/nature12278

**Used for:** The result that K-feldspar dominates mineral dust ice nucleation and is active several degrees warmer than clays. Used here only as the source of a directional ordering check, not of any coefficient.

## Hiranuma et al. (2015)

`hiranuma2015` · access: **verbatim** · open access

Hiranuma, N., et al. (2015). A comprehensive laboratory study on the immersion freezing behavior of illite NX particles: a comparison of 17 ice nucleation measurement techniques. Atmospheric Chemistry and Physics 15, 4823-4849. doi:10.5194/acp-15-4823-2015

<https://acp.copernicus.org/articles/15/4823/2015/>

**Used for:** Basis for the size of the BET-vs-geometric surface area discrepancy for clay samples, and for the roughly one order of magnitude spread between techniques measuring the same material.

## Koop et al. (2000)

`koop2000` · access: **verbatim** · paywalled

Koop, T., Luo, B., Tsias, A., Peter, T. (2000). Water activity as the determinant for homogeneous ice nucleation in aqueous solutions. Nature 406, 611-614. doi:10.1038/35020537

**Used for:** Cited for the direction of the solute effect: dissolved salts lower water activity and therefore depress freezing rather than promote it. INA-sim does not implement the water-activity shift; it states the direction and declines to score solutes as ice nucleants.

## CRC Handbook (2023)

`crc_handbook` · access: **textbook** · paywalled

Rumble, J. R. (ed.) (2023). CRC Handbook of Chemistry and Physics, 104th edition. CRC Press.

**Used for:** Cryoscopic constant of water Kf = 1.86 K kg mol^-1 and the molar masses used by the colligative freezing-point-depression model.
